entries.title: Nike au Centre Pompidou
entries.format: 2024 Olympics-era exhibition and brand campaign spanning social assets, signage, posters, merch, and façade-scale motion
entries.why: A strong campaign-visual reference because the case study shows how one promotional system can stay unmistakably Nike while flexing from tiny event touchpoints to the largest screen in Europe. The system couples compressed display type, a tight orange-and-Volt palette, frontal athlete photography, and one pattern thread so the campaign stays legible even when formats, durations, and viewing distances change radically.
entries.implementationFormat: Event-scale campaign visual system with environmental graphics, social crops, and motion-led OOH

entries.title: Think it. Make it.
entries.format: 2024 global brand-awareness campaign spanning OOH, transit placements, social crops, and an animated anthem
entries.why: A strong campaign-visual reference because it shows how a famously minimal software brand can temporarily widen its visual language for public media without losing recognition. The system keeps Notion's illustration DNA, then adds close-profile crops, primary-color blocks, bespoke headlines, and one simple call-to-action so the campaign reads clearly from billboards down to phone-sized social posts.
entries.implementationFormat: Global brand-awareness campaign system for a software brand across outdoor, transit, social, and motion media

entries.title: Pepsi "Crave"
entries.format: Global beverage campaign centered on a 30-second hero film and a reusable liquid-footage asset library for regional content
entries.why: A strong campaign-visual reference because the BUCK case is not just a polished one-off film. It documents a campaign system built from practical liquid shots, motion-control capture, and swappable pack assets that Pepsi teams could reuse across markets. That makes it useful for studying how a sensory hero concept can become a modular global rollout kit rather than a single locked edit.
entries.implementationFormat: Global beverage campaign system built from hero-film footage, localization-ready packshots, and downstream regional derivatives

entries.title: DEMO 2025
entries.maker: Studio Dumbar/DEPT® with Global, blowUP media, adtrackmedia, StandardVision, VLGE, and Macron
entries.format: Global motion-design festival identity spanning public screens, an interactive digital universe, sound, and wearable merchandise
entries.why: A strong campaign-visual reference because DEMO 2025 treats a festival identity as a distributed promotional system rather than a single event poster or film. Studio Dumbar/DEPT® carries one visual grammar from a distorted globe and blue RGB-cycle color into bespoke public-screen dimensions, a ten-world digital extension, a sonic library, and a limited-edition jersey. The evidence is useful for studying how a motion-first campaign stays recognizable while scaling across cities, screens, web, and physical merchandise.
entries.implementationFormat: Global festival campaign system connecting public-screen motion, curated content, an interactive web extension, sound, and merchandise

assets.notes: Nike's house typography is stretched and condensed into bolder poster-like expressions instead of being replaced outright.
assets.reuse: Escalate the existing type system before inventing a detached event face.

assets.notes: Orange remains the anchor while Volt green supplies short-term campaign energy.
assets.reuse: Keep palette decisions extremely narrow when the campaign already has strong type and imagery.

assets.notes: Direct portraits and customized AI-generated shoes create blunt hero frames that survive from social to architecture.
assets.reuse: Favor frontal portraits when distance and speed of reading matter more than narrative scene-building.

assets.notes: The Electric Print motif creates one shared textural thread between product, motion, and environmental materials.
assets.reuse: Carry one recognizable texture across the entire rollout to reduce the number of visual variables each format needs.

assets.notes: A short master tagline plus tailored sub-headlines turns a flexible product story into public-facing copy that reads quickly.
assets.reuse: Create one master imperative and derive concise variations instead of writing unrelated campaign headlines per channel.

assets.notes: Roman Muradov's illustrations remain the campaign's recognizability engine, but the tighter head-and-shoulders crops make them carry more emotional and narrative weight.
assets.reuse: Keep the signature illustration author while changing framing before replacing the visual language entirely.

assets.notes: The system adds saturated yellow, blue, and red blocks to a previously monochrome brand so the work can compete in cities and transit systems.
assets.reuse: Use a limited temporary palette as a campaign-only amplifier when the master brand is too quiet for OOH.

assets.notes: Simple geometric color fields and framing blocks give the hand-drawn imagery enough structure to scale cleanly across placements.
assets.reuse: Pair expressive illustration with blunt framing geometry so the campaign still reads as a system under heavy resizing and recropping.

assets.notes: Custom-shot liquid footage provides the campaign's core emotional and visual payoff, functioning as both a cinematic centerpiece and modular raw material.
assets.reuse: Invest in a few unforgettable physical captures when the product's appeal depends on texture, force, or refreshment.

assets.notes: Pack shots are built to support logo replacement while maintaining consistent ice, condensation, and appetite cues.
assets.reuse: Separate product realism from market-specific branding so the same campaign base can travel globally.

assets.notes: The preserved wet surface treatment keeps every derivative asset feeling cold and tactile even after brand swapping and recropping.
assets.reuse: Treat surface detail as a system requirement, not just a finishing flourish, when the campaign is selling refreshment.

assets.notes: The playful globe gives the expanded festival footprint a single visual shorthand that can move between still compositions, motion, and spatial scenes.
assets.reuse: Build one recognizable geometric subject that can deform, rotate, crop, or flatten while retaining the campaign's identity.

assets.notes: The DEMO logo and typography remain central while the surrounding identity evolves across media and editions.
assets.reuse: Protect one high-salience wordmark or type lockup as the stable layer in a system that otherwise invites experimentation.

assets.notes: The selected motion works form a large content library, with many pieces specifically created for the physical screen dimensions of each location.
assets.reuse: Plan a content pipeline and curation rule when the campaign needs hundreds of variations, rather than treating every asset as an isolated hero piece.

assets.notes: The team developed a sonic library alongside motion tests, balancing ethereal and spacious textures with heavier, more rhythmic influences.
assets.reuse: Develop sound with the visual motion system so audio can reinforce the same pacing and emotional contrast across cutdowns.

assets.notes: The Macron collaboration turns the festival identity into wearable art and gives the campaign a portable, non-screen touchpoint.
assets.reuse: Choose one physical extension that compresses the campaign grammar into an object people can carry beyond the media placement.

motion.title: Architectural motion as the headline expression
motion.notes: Punchy motion graphics turn the Pompidou façade into a campaign billboard, making animation part of the main identity rather than a secondary adaptation.
motion.fallback: If architectural motion is unavailable, keep the same type compression, palette, and portrait framing in static OOH key art.

motion.title: Motion language stays sharp across shorter outputs
motion.notes: The studio describes a dynamic motion approach built for many touchpoints over the two-week run, implying short-form animated derivatives rather than one single hero film.
motion.fallback: Preserve the same abrupt type tension and palette contrast in static crops when motion time or budget drops away.

motion.title: Animated anthem translates the static grammar into motion
motion.notes: BUCK describes an animated anthem that pulls the close crops, color palette, and conceptual storytelling into one succinct moving brand story for the launch.
motion.fallback: If a launch cannot fund a hero film, keep the same profile crops, color blocks, and imperative headline structure in static OOH and social frames.

motion.title: High-speed motion control turns refreshment into spectacle
motion.notes: The moving image language depends on slow-motion collisions, splashes, and propelled liquid events captured through specialized rigs and cameras.
motion.fallback: If this level of production is unavailable, keep the same appetite logic through fewer but sharper practical shots instead of replacing everything with generic CG motion.

motion.title: Motion follows a clear crave-to-satisfaction progression
motion.notes: BUCK describes an emotional arc of crave, consumption, and satisfaction, which makes the edit feel like a campaign story rather than a disconnected reel of pretty liquid shots.
motion.fallback: Even in short cutdowns, preserve a simple tension-release sequence so the motion still communicates a product feeling.

motion.title: Loops are composed for attention in public space
motion.notes: The event places motion artworks into advertising-screen infrastructure, turning normally transactional displays into an immersive 24-hour gallery across many cities.
motion.fallback: For reduced-motion or low-bandwidth contexts, keep the globe, type, and RGB-cycle palette in a still or gently crossfaded composition with a clear DEMO lockup.

motion.title: Letterforms become characters in a spatial digital extension
motion.notes: The ten DEMOverse worlds populate their scenes with walking DEMO letters, making the identity's typography an active participant in the environment.
motion.fallback: If a 3D world is unavailable, preserve the same sense of exploration through a sequence of curated scenes or a horizontal reel with simple keyboard and touch navigation.

motion.title: Sound is developed in parallel with motion tests
motion.notes: The sonic identity evolves with the motion experiments, layering spacious atmospheres and textured rhythms to give different screen pieces a coherent emotional range.
motion.fallback: Make the campaign understandable without audio through timing, contrast, and typography; use sound as reinforcement rather than the only carrier of meaning.

interactions.title: Browse the motion collection through thematic worlds
interactions.reuse: Use a navigable archive when a campaign's content volume and spatial logic benefit from discovery rather than a single linear landing-page scroll.
